english.starts_with: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said:
english.ends_with: Sulayman al-Taymi said: It means raise your hand in supplication toward your chest.\n\n

prior_review_continuity.prior_statement_en: Competing non-slaughter readings connect wanhar with placing the right hand over the left at the upper chest, raising the hands in prayer, or facing the qibla with the chest; these are retained as attributed alternatives.
prior_review_continuity.prior_voice_name: Ali, Muhammad ibn Kab, Ibn Abbas, Abu Salih and other named authorities
prior_review_continuity.required_refinement: Replace the mixed voice cluster with eight bounded evidence units. Preserve direct, passive and chained report markers; distinguish Ibn al-A'rabi the lexicographer from Ibn al-Arabi the jurist; do not infer a full oral route or Qurtubi adoption.

atomic_voice_units.arabic_anchor: وقال علي ... ومحمد بن كعب ... ضع اليمنى على اليسرى حذاء النحر في الصلاة . وروي عن ابن عباس أيضا
وروي عن علي أيضا ... يرفع يديه في التكبير إلى نحره . وكذا قال جعفر بن علي ... يرفع يديه أول ما يكبر للإحرام إلى النحر
وعن علي ... لما نزلت ... قال النبي ... لجبريل ... وإن زينة الصلاة رفع اليدين عند كل تكبيرة
وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال : استقبل القبلة بنحرك ; وقاله الفراء والكلبي وأبو الأحوص
قال الفراء : سمعت بعض العرب يقول : منازلنا تتناحر ; أي تتقابل
وقال ابن الأعرابي : هو انتصاب الرجل في الصلاة بإزاء المحراب
atomic_voice_units.disambiguation: Ibn al-A'rabi (ابن الأعرابي) is not Ibn al-Arabi (ابن العربي), the Maliki jurist quoted earlier.

arabic.source_text: قال الفراء : سمعت بعض العرب يقول : منازلنا تتناحر ; أي تتقابل ، نحر هذا بنحر هذا ; أي قبالته .

english.source_text: Al-Farra' said: I heard some Arabs say: Our dwellings face one another; meaning they confront each other—this one's front facing that one's; meaning opposite to it.

source_anchors.locator: Surah 108:2 displayed line 10; volume 20 printed page 195
source_anchors.supports: Al-Qurtubi attributes the lexical example to al-Farra, who says he heard some unnamed Arabs use تناحر of dwellings facing one another; the page's editorial note records variant readings in al-Farra and Lisan al-Arab.

source_anchors.locator: volume 14, root نحر, printed page 209; displayed lines 592-599
source_anchors.supports: The lexicon records dwellings/places facing one another under تناحر and quotes an al-Farra attribution; supports the sense تتقابل / facing one another, not the chain of Qurtubi's tafsir report.
Exact stored Arabic witness and stable row MD5.
English translates the example as dwellings facing one another, matching the Arabic sense.

attribution_boundary.relation: Qurtubi reports al-Farra's lexical testimony; al-Farra says he heard unnamed speakers use the expression.

arabic.source_text: وقال ابن الأعرابي : هو انتصاب الرجل في الصلاة بإزاء المحراب ; من قولهم : منازلهم تتناحر ; أي تتقابل .

english.source_text: Ibn al-A'rabi said: It is the standing upright of a man in prayer opposite the mihrab; from their saying: their dwellings face one another; meaning they confront each other.

source_anchors.locator: Surah 108:2, first issue, displayed line 10; volume 20, printed page 195.
source_anchors.supports: The Qurtubi text says Ibn al-A'rabi attributes the lexical definition of standing in prayer opposite the mihrab; the following clause gives the dwellings-facing-one-another example. The passive Ata report begins separately after this unit.

source_anchors.locator: Volume 14, root نحر, printed page 209, displayed lines 598-599.
source_anchors.supports: The dictionary first explains نحر الرجل في الصلاة as standing upright and raising the chest, then explicitly attributes النحرة انتصاب الرجل في الصلاة بإزاء المحراب to Ibn al-A'rabi. It corroborates the lexical wording, but does not establish direct copying or an oral route to Qurtubi.

source_anchors.locator: Article “Ibn al-A'rabi (d. 231 AH),” displayed lines 201-216 and 230-231.
source_anchors.supports: Identifies him as Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn al-A'rabi and describes him as a grammarian and lexicographer; gives death in 231 AH (also records a reported 230 AH variant).

source_anchors.locator: Article heading and identity lines 66-71; bibliographic identification lines 95-111; discussion of legal scholarship and Qur'anic commentary lines 138 onward.
source_anchors.supports: Identifies Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi as a distinct Andalusi Maliki jurist and commentator, d. 543/1148. The name is ابن العربي, unlike lexicographer ابن الأعرابي.
Exact Arabic attribution, definition, and lexical example; row hash recorded above.
English rendering preserves the same named lexicographer, posture, mihrab location, explanatory example, and boundary before the separate Ata report.

attribution_boundary.not_the_jurist: Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi al-Ma'afiri (ابن العربي), distinct person and spelling form

variant_and_provenance_handling.lisan_wording_overlap: Ibn Manzur's Lisan al-Arab preserves the same lexical definition under نحر and names Ibn al-A'rabi.

bounded_revalidation_q07f.decision: The bounded Arabic and English spans align. The lexical authority is Ibn al-A'rabi (Muhammad ibn Ziyad, lexicographer), not the Maliki jurist Ibn al-Arabi. Lisan al-Arab independently corroborates the wording; no isnad, direct borrowing, Qurtubi adoption, authenticity judgment, or variant edition is inferred. No database correction is proposed.
